title: Community planning permits, Get READI Plan and station-area zoning
subtitle: Uptown BIA lease renewal, funding request review for a community organization, encampment legislation briefing, and new mixed-use zone near ION stations.
overview: Council approved the City's first Get READI Plan, which sets goals for reconciliation, equity, accessibility, diversity and inclusion across City services and workplaces {{vote:m5}}. Staff will return in February 2025 with a report on which community organizations the City currently funds and how future operating-funding requests should be handled. That report will include a review of a request from the Coalition of Muslim Women KW {{vote:m6}}.

Council also directed staff to consult the public on a draft Community Planning Permit By-law and urban design guidelines for Uptown and the Herb Street corridor {{vote:m4}}. The system is meant to combine zoning, site plan and minor variance approvals into one faster process. A new Station Area Mixed-Use zone was approved for lands near the Research and Technology Park and Northfield ION stations {{vote:m7}}. It allows housing alongside employment and commercial uses. Council also renewed the Uptown BIA's lease at the Waterloo City Centre {{vote:m3}}.

Council met in closed session before the public meeting. The minutes record no public report of decisions from it. A councillor asked for a briefing note in the new year on the province's proposed Safer Municipalities Act and its effect on encampments.

decisions.detail: Council gave final approval to the City's first plan for reconciliation, equity, accessibility, diversity and inclusion, as presented in report CAO2024-029.
Staff will report back in February 2025 on which community organizations the City funds and on principles for future requests, including a review of the Coalition of Muslim Women KW request.
Council received the report and directed staff to consult the public and interested parties on the draft Community Planning Permit By-law and urban design guidelines.
Council approved the new Station Area Mixed-Use zone and related amendments to Zoning By-law 2018-050, applying it to lands near two ION station areas.
Council approved renewing the Uptown BIA's lease at the Waterloo City Centre under the terms in report COM2024-046 and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the amending agreement.

debate: On the BIA lease, one councillor asked whether the BIA's place in City Hall was secure. Staff said the lease allows relocation only for an operational need, with about six months' notice and the tenant's agreement, and that no move is planned.

On the planning permit system, councillors asked about site plan review for developments of fewer than 10 units, infill next to existing homes, and the role of the Committee of Adjustment. Consultants said the system can cover small developments and that the by-law sets its own thresholds for variations and notice. Mail-outs would go to properties within 120 metres for variations beyond the standard.

One councillor questioned the word 'character' in the design guidelines because it often causes disputes. Staff offered to define it more clearly or use a term such as 'sense of place'. Councillors also urged wide consultation, including west-side neighbourhood associations.

On the Get READI Plan, councillors asked about risks and implementation. Staff named the current social and political climate and strained household budgets as the biggest risk, and said the implementation plan would build trust through regular reporting. Councillors also asked about faster ways to improve accessibility in older buildings, and staff said a report is expected around April.

A delegate from the Coalition of Muslim Women KW asked for stable operating funding in place of project-based grants. Councillors debated whether the staff report should cover only current funding or also principles for future requests, and chose to include both. One councillor wanted the motion kept separate from the Get READI Plan.

On the new zone, one councillor said noise, vibration and land-use compatibility studies must be considered before the holding provision is lifted, to protect existing industrial employers. Another asked why child care is an ancillary use. Staff said this follows the official plan and that the rules are flexible.
